questions.question: If cos q + sin q = 31 _________ 25 , then what will be the value of cos 2q ? यदि cos q + sin q = 31 _________ 25 है, तो cos 2q का मान कितना होगा?

If cos q + sin q =

From (1) and (2):

2 cos q = 48/25

cos q = 24/25

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I used to swim across the river when I was young.

questions.question: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Latika said to him, "I got a hefty discount on this television."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Latika said to him, "I got a hefty discount on this television."

options.text: Latika told him that she has got a hefty discount on that television.
options.html: Latika told him that she has got a hefty discount on that television.

options.text: Latika told him that she is getting a hefty discount on that television.

options.text: Latika told him that she has got a hefty discount on this television.
options.html: Latika told him that she has got a hefty discount on this television.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

For example:

He said, "Arya sent me a book." (Direct Speech)

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to him' will be changed to 'told him'.

'This television' will be changed to 'that television'.

Therefore, the correct answer is (c): Latika told him that she had got a hefty discount on that television.

questions.question: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The new owners hired a lot of new servers.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The new owners hired a lot of new servers.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is (a): A lot of new servers were hired by the new owners.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Had they not cleared the exam?

options.html: Had the exam not been cleared by them?

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like: have, has, had.

The format of such a sentence in Active voice is: Have/Has/Had + Subject + V3 + Object?

Therefore, in Passive voice, the format will be: Have/Has/Had + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)?

For example:

Has Rohit written the letter? (Active)

Has the letter been written by Rohit? (Passive)

Since 'exam' is a singular noun, it cannot be preceded by (in interrogative sentence) plural verb 'have'.

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is (d): Had the exam not been cleared by them?

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. P. In Tokyo, they built an expressway linking the international airport in Haneda to the centre and widened some of the city's major arteries. Q. These infrastructure improvements helped to bring about the Japanese economic miracle over the next couple of decades. R. Tokyo 2020 was supposed to be a great economic stimulus, replicating the achievements of Tokyo 1964. S. It was thanks to hosting the Olympics that Japan invested in infrastructure such as the famous Shinkansen bullet train.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P. In Tokyo, they built an expressway linking the international airport in Haneda to the centre and widened some of the city's major arteries.

Q. These infrastructure improvements helped to bring about the Japanese economic miracle over the next couple of decades.

R. Tokyo 2020 was supposed to be a great economic stimulus, replicating the achievements of Tokyo 1964.

S. It was thanks to hosting the Olympics that Japan invested in infrastructure such as the famous Shinkansen bullet train.
questions.solution:
Sentence R comes first as it introduces the topic of the passage - 'economic stimulus in Japan'.

Sentence S comes next and explains that the fact that Japan was hosting the Olympics made it invest in the infrastructure project - the Shinkansen bullet train.

Sentence P comes next and mentions another infrastructure project.

'These infrastructure developments' refer to the Shinkansen bullet train and expressway mentioned in sentences S and P respectively.

So, the correct order is RSPQ.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

The blank requires an adjective to denote teenagers' state with respect to academic stress. So, option (d) 'resistance' (a noun) is eliminated.

When 'scared + preposition' is followed by the thing that scares someone, the preposition generally used is 'of', not 'to' (that follows the blank). So, option (a) is incorrect.

Liable - responsible by law; legally answerable. The statement does not imply that it is the responsibility of teenagers to take stress. So, option (c) is not correct.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

Physical - relating to the body as opposed to the mind.

The sentence with the third blank discusses the type of solutions that are required to deal with academic stress.

Here, words like 'collateral', 'convention', and 'physical' do not fit in contextually.

'Intervention solutions' would imply the direct involvement of those trying to help students with academic stress.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

The blank requires a noun to denote what everyone wants to avoid in their life. 'Sneak' (move or go in a furtive or stealthy way) does not fit in contextually.

The sentence implies that people do not want to fail any exam. So, saying that they want to avoid purpose does not fit in the context of the passage.

'Wanderlust' (which means 'a strong desire to travel') does not fit in the context of the passage.

Filling the blank with 'ambiguity' (means 'a situation or statement that is unclear because it can be understood in more than one way') implies that people want to avoid unclear situations in their life.

This fits in contextually.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.
